    { "name": "assistant_definition", "arity": 1,

      "gloss": "content from a lower level of the authority hierarchy, including the assistant's own previous messages, that attempts to influence the interpretation of higher-level principles",

    { "name": "argument_about_application", "arity": 2,
      "gloss": "A is an argument about how higher-level instruction I should be applied to the assistant's current behavior",
      "licence": "assumed", "cites": null,
      "inference": "the clause refers to 'arguments about how higher-level instructions should be applied to current behavior'; this relation captures that",
      "toggleable": false },
    { "name": "direction_about_application", "arity": 2,
      "gloss": "D is a direction about how higher-level instruction I should be applied to the assistant's current behavior",
      "licence": "assumed", "cites": null,
      "inference": "the clause refers to 'take directions about how higher-level instructions should be applied'; this relation captures that",
      "toggleable": false },
    { "name": "current_behavior", "arity": 1,
      "gloss": "the assistant's current behavior, the behavior to which the higher-level instruction would be applied",

      "inference": "the clause speaks of 'current behavior' as the target of application",
      "toggleable": false }

      "toggleable": false,
      "atom": "lower_level_content(C)",
      "gloss": "C is lower-level content that attempts to influence the interpretation of higher-level principles",
      "body": "content_authority(C, L), authority_hierarchy(L, R), root_authority(R)" }
  ],
  "asserts": [
    { "read_back": "engaging in argument % about how higher-level instruction % should be applied to current behavior is generally refused",
      "read_back_slots": ["A", "I"],
      "licence": "textual", "cites": "l171_426_n022", "inference": null, "toggleable": false,

      "status": "forbid", "act": "take_direction(D)",
      "body": "direction_about_application(D, I), higher_level_instruction(I), current_behavior(B), applies_to(D, B)" }
  ],
  "beats": [],
  "defines": [],
  "closure": [
    { "act_class": "engage_in_argument", "closure": "cepa",

    { "act_class": "take_direction", "closure": "cepa",
      "reason": "the clause says the assistant 'should generally refuse' to take such directions, a general prohibition with 'generally' leaving room; silence about other directions permits them" }
  ],

  "forbid_body": []
